utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Oric, good morning to you. Can you follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, gentlemen. Yes, I can follow the proceedings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I'm Patricia Sellers representing the Office of the Prosecution. With me today is co-counsel Mr. Gramsci Di Fazio. Our case manager is Donnica Henry-Frijlink, and also we have Ms. Djurdja Mirkovic, who is also our assistant case manager today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Sellers. And good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I am Vasvija Vidovic, together with Mr. John Jones, we are defending Mr. Naser Oric. And we have our legal assistant, or case manager, Ms. Jasmina Cosic and our case manager, Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic. Good morning to you and your team. Any preliminaries before we bring in Mr. Eric?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: There are no preliminaries before this witness, but there is a matter that we should raise before the following witness, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I suppose you raise it afterwards or --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. It's fine with us, and we wouldn't want to hold up this next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Eric, and welcome back to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You know the procedure, so -- already.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Usher is going to give you the text of the solemn declaration. Please read it out aloud and that's your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. Yes. We start with Ms. Sellers. The reason why you have been recalled, Mr. Eric, is that we have come by video recording which provides some information which you would have certainly been questioned upon had we seen this video before. Having seen it now, we need to have you questioned on some aspects that emerge from this video. The Prosecution is going first, and then the Defence will follow. Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Examined by Ms. Sellers:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning. Would you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: My name is Slavisa Eric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And isn't it correct that you testified before this Tribunal before Their Honours in the Prosecution versus Naser Oric on the 26th of October?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Eric, you testified surrounding the events of the Muslim attack against the village of Kravica on the 7th of January, 1993 and then its recapture by Bosnian Serb forces on the 15th of March, 1993. Were you ever asked about those events by a film crew?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I was, I think, in 1994, for television Zvornik. I gave a brief statement about the suffering of the village. They were collecting or gathering material about the destruction of those villages and how repairs are were being under way and so on. So I was called. At that time, I was the head of the medical services in the Bratunac Brigade. So then I went and gave them a statement. This was in Kravica, in a house which was a kind of local coffee bar. And I gave a statement to the local television. But there were several of us, and we all gave statements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please explain to the Trial Chamber who else was with you or interviewed when you were being interviewed by this film crew from Zvornik Television.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Jovan Nikolic was there, Ratko Nikolic, Goran Djuric, a friend of mine, Mira Djukanovic, myself. I don't know if anyone else was there. I cannot remember. It's possible that some other people were there also. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you have a chance to see a broadcast of this film by Zvornik Television when it was first put on the air, first broadcast?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you recently shown a copy of that broadcast by the office -- in the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would like to have the exhibit that's previously been marked P44 placed on our screens. Your Honour, this is -- I'm sorry, 448. This will be the video. And I just want to make one statement for the record. I previously discussed this with Defence counsel. The videotape is quite long. We are interested in what we refer to as segment 2, which concerns the TV show. Segment 1 concerns other events that are no relationship to the witness who is before us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's up to you. We are not going to interfere in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Fine. One last announcement before showing this tape is that I want to inform both the Trial Chamber and Defence counsel that there are subtitles. There are English subtitles that the Office of the Prosecution has placed on the tape. They are draft. We are sending it out for final translation. There will be final subtitles. And I will note that the Office of the Prosecutor has found a couple of errors in the translation. So I just want to state that openly on the record so that the Trial Chamber and Defence are both aware. Okay. Now turning to the video.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, would you look at the screen before you, in front of you. Was this the beginning of the television programme?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell Their Honours what it says.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Serbian Television Zvornik. Before these were the letters on the registration plates in Zvornik, ZV. And then it says "the hidden truth crimes against Serbs from 1992 to 1995." That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go to the next image. Mr. Eric, can you look at this carefully and please tell the Trial Chamber: Is this part of the Zvornik TV programme, and what is written there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It says: "Serbian Television Zvornik. We apologise to the viewers because of the bad quality of the tape, because these are tapes on VHS cassettes. We invite all the viewers who were detained in Muslim prisons, and those who have some kind of video cassettes, photographs, or other material which we could use for this hidden truth, Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond crimes against Serbs from 1992 to 1995. And could they please contact us on telephone number 583-710, or come to Television Zvornik. Thank you for your understanding."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think we might ask that the lights could be dimmed just a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what I meant when I said -- I didn't mean to shut you or anyone else down. Yes. I think that would help. That would help. Thank you. Yes. Move ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Okay. Could we now go to the next clip, portion of this television show. And could we have the sound, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I'd like to have the sound to this, because I'd like the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I would imagine they heard you, because they rewound a little bit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, does that video show an accurate representation of what you said when you were interviewed by Zvornik Television?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone tell you what to say that day?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you reading from a prepared text?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: It's possible that I had jotted down a couple of the names of the people in order to remember. The people that we were bringing out that day. It's possible that I wrote down two, three, four of those names. There were a lot of wounded, so I didn't want to get confused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in the video, you stated that you were waiting for helicopters during the attack. Now, from your knowledge --

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- were you waiting for helicopters to come to Kravica in order to attack the Muslim soldiers?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. They told us that helicopters could come. They had apparently promised them from Bratunac, that helicopters would come to evacuate these wounded people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those helicopters ever come and evacuate the wounded people?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would ask that we just go back to the clip showing Mr. Eric again and just -- so we can see what he's wearing, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Eric, would you please take a look again at the image, and would you explain to the Trial Chamber: What were you wearing that day in the video clip?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, you can see I was wearing a white T-shirt, I was wearing a camouflage shirt, and I was wearing one-piece suit, camouflage, and also -- overalls, and I was also wearing a sleeveless jacket, waistcoat. So I had four layers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this a complete uniform?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was that uniform issued to you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: In late 1993 or early 1994. This is all recorded in the Bratunac Brigade command when these overalls arrived. I think there is a list and there must be a date when this was issued to me. I still have those overalls, and when it's very cold - I have it at home - when it's very cold, I put it on, if I'm working on something and it's winter. So I still have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this what you were wearing the day of the Muslim attack on Kravica, 7th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. I told you earlier: I was issued it in 1993 or 1994. On the day of the attack, however, I was wearing a sweater, civilian sweater, on an olive-drab shirt, trousers which were of the same olive-drab colour, civilian boots, and I also had an olive-drab jacket from the former Yugoslav army. And I put that on before I went out. But up until that moment, I was just wearing trousers and a shirt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, how do you remember what you were wearing the day of the Kravica attack?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: For the next 15 to 20 days, I actually had no other clothes than the ones I was wearing when I went out. That's what I wore. Since all my documents stayed behind in the house - my driver's licence, my car registration, papers, my personal ID - I had to get duplicates. So I have that photograph. I know exactly the clothes that I had when I left. And I wore those clothes for a long time, until I was given something else to wear. I had nothing else to wear. Everything had been burned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are you testifying that you renewed your driver's licence and personal documents after the attack and you were wearing the same clothes when you renewed those documents that you'd been wearing the day of the attack against Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take a photo when you were renewing some of your personal documents, such as your driver's licence?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. This was seven to eight days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask at this time two things. We're going to put an exhibit on Sanction's screen. I will be asking for a P number, but also at the request of Defence counsel, I was going to ask Mr. Eric to produce his driver's licence, available for Madam Vidovic to look at. But can we first pass out these documents. Now, Mr. Eric, do you recognise the document that's on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. That is my driver's licence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you give an original copy of your driver's licence to the Office of the Prosecutor on Sunday?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was a copy made of your driver's licence?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you consider this an accurate copy of the driver's licence that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would now ask if we could take a closer look at the photo on the driver's licence. Excuse me. I must ask also that we don't enter his driver's licence into evidence or -- he will not be able to drive when he gets back, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the Trial Chamber was shown the original driving licence of the witness, which the exhibit -- what number are we going to give this, Mr. Registrar? 462? 461?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 462. Of which Exhibit P462 is a photocopy.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I will be tendering that into evidence at the conclusion of these questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, would you please look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Mr. Jones or Madam Vidovic, are you satisfied that this is a true photocopy of the original driving licence?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, would you look at the picture that's on this screen. Now, are these the clothes that you were wearing on the day of the attack against Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender the copy of the driver's licence at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. As stated, this will be P462.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, could you please also tell us: What date did you Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond acquire this driver's licence?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: 15 or 16 days after Kravica burned down. I think it says here, the 21st of January, 1993. So 14 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you also mentioned that you were wearing a coat on the day of the attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would ask that the next exhibit be placed on Sanction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the sort of jacket that I had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, is this the type of coat that used to be issued by the JNA army?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, because people are wearing that type coat --

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: I didn't get that one from the JNA. We just got it. The JNA brought it over and it was given to people. This is the sort of uniform that they used in the army earlier on. Since it was cold, I got this jacket to protect myself from the cold.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this jacket issued by the JNA prior to the Kravica attack because you were part of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. Before. Before. I'm not sure when, nor did one really sign for these. You know, they just brought them there and then you took whichever size was right for you. There were about 50 other perhaps 100 of these, as well as other items of clothing that people could just take and use, such as trousers, boots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like Mr. Eric to look at the next clip on the video, and the Trial Chamber also, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. He's my uncle, Ratko Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this person also filmed by Zvornik Television at the same time that you were filmed?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you present when this part of the video was made?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you stated that he was your uncle. Would you please explain to the Trial Chamber exactly how he's related to you.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: My mother's sister is his wife. My mother's sister is his wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know whether Ratko Nikolic was using a prepared text when he was speaking to the television station?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. No. None of us did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was forced to say what he said that day in the cafe while he was being interviewed by the television station?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Can we please see the next clip.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: I know. This is a person from Jezestica. I think he's now very sick. He had a stroke or something like that. He can no longer move. I know this person, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know this person's name?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Miladin. Miladin Bogdanovic. Yes, he's from Jezestica. I know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he also filmed on the same day by Zvornik TV that you were filmed?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you present when this part of the video was made?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'll ask you once again: To your knowledge, was he using a prepared text?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. No. But there was nothing that was prepared for us to use.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Can we go to the next clip, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, I'd ask you to look again and please tell the Trial Chamber if you know this person.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a very good friend of mine, Goran Djuric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this also filmed on the same day that you were filmed by Zvornik TV?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, the same day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you present when this segment of the TV show was filmed?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again I ask you: Was this person, to your knowledge, forced to say what he said that day in the cafe to the television station?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'd like to ask for the next clip of the film, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it important to hear this person's --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I was going to ask a couple of questions about what this person said. The others were more for identification purposes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Just that? Just that? You're just going to limit yourself to asking the witness what this person is saying?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Identification of the person --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Plus what he's saying, not beyond that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we just put a freeze-shot of the person. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Eric, did you know the person who we just saw on the clip there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't get the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can I ask you to repeat the name of that person, please, Mr. Eric.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Jovan Nikolic. I know him very well. He is a relative of mine, or rather, my father's relative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this also filmed by the Zvornik TV the same time that you and the other men you've just identified were filmed, and were you also present when this --

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present when this portion of the TV show was --

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this portion, Mr. Jovan Nikolic spoke about communications between Milici and Kravica. Could you explain to the Trial Chamber from your knowledge what types of communications existed between Milici and Kravica during this time period of 1992, prior to or during the attack on Kravica.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: What I know of is that we went from Kravica to Milici two or three times, across through Siljkovici, Kostan, Ravni Buljin, Rogac, Milici. I'm really not that familiar with the area. They went there to discuss the linking up of the line at Buljim. I think that was the reason for them going. Once or twice, I think, they went. It's a difficult road to travel. They used a lorry to go, or a military jeep. It's some sort of a forest road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever go to Milici from Kravica yourself with this group that you're describing as "they would go"?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. No. No. No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who would go to Milici from Kravica that you knew of? Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: I can't remember the specific people who did go. Maybe Jole was one of the people with them. Probably there was a driver who was part of the group, but I can't be certain. Therefore, it's very difficult for me to say. I didn't really memorise that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people that you just mentioned, were they part of village guards at Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were there reinforcements that came from Milici to help the village guards in Kravica on the 7th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. They never came. They set out to help us, but they were ambushed at Kostan and they couldn't get through. We heard sounds of shooting. This went on for about half an hour and then it stopped. We knew that they had not broken through. That was once we had set out towards Opravdici on our way to the Drina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is Kostan, one of the places that you testified about earlier, where ambushes would happen?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an area where Muslims were crossing from Srebrenica across Kostan and Konjevic Polje, Cerska and on to Tuzla. It was an undefended corridor. It wasn't controlled by anyone. On from Buljim and towards Siljkovici, between Siljkovici and Buljim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please show the next clip.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Eric, were you present when this part of the TV show was filmed?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. This is footage that was taken at the Kravica school. I know where this footage was taken but I wasn't there personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that Jovan Nikolic again of -- again who was speaking on that segment?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified earlier that Jovan Nikolic had been injured at the attack on Glogova on the 24th of December, 1992. Are those the injuries that he's referring to in this part of the clip?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that he was not present during the attack on Kravica on the 7th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't. He was seriously wounded and he was receiving treatment for quite a long time after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you: Have you ever seen a video cassette of Kravica that filmed the area soon after the January 7th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. My attention is being drawn to the fact that in the transcript, you have suddenly, or at least recent time been transformed from who you are to Ms. Richardson, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: It's the brains, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, probably that's it. So could we have -- I know that now it's past, you can't correct the transcript on screen now, but I suppose for the record, I'm just mentioning it wherever there is Ms. Richardson it should be replaced by Ms. Sellers. Okay? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, have you ever seen a video cassette that was -- or that shows Kravica soon after the attack on Kravica on the 7th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw this tape. I'm just not sure when. I think someone brought it from Srebrenica. But I can't remember when.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see this tape before you were filmed by the Zvornik TV station?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: I can't be sure about that. I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see a copy of this video cassette when you looked at the film of the Zvornik TV station in the Office of the Prosecutor a couple of days ago?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did this video cassette, was it part of the Zvornik TV programme?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you tell, when you first saw that video cassette, or when you saw it recently, whether it was a video cassette taken possibly by a Bosnian Muslim or a Bosnian Serb?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: It could not have been taken by the Serbs. That tape, I think it was in January 1993 that it was taken, and there were no Serbs in Kravica at the time. Therefore, it would not have been possible for Serbs to have taken that footage. It must have been the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would ask the case manager now to place that part of the Zvornik TV show before our screens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, would you look at just a couple of those images and tell the Trial Chamber whether you can tell if that's part of the Zvornik TV show.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. I've already seen this section.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could we continue it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. There was this background music. I can't remember the name of the performer now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this music that is typically Bosnian Muslim music or Bosnian Serb music?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: For the most part, this would be typical of Bosnian Muslims. This was taken from the direction of Konjevic Polje, so now you pass Sandici on the way to Kravica and then on to Bratunac. I'm talking about the specific portion of the footage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Can we continue a little bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sveta Milanovic's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber if you recognise any image before us now.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Some sort of a car there and a kiosk. There was a checkpoint there, and you couldn't get through and continue on to Sandici. There was some sort of a cabin here that the guards used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that a village guard checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are we entering into the village of Kravica and the direction that this film is moving?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. From Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could we continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could you stop for one second, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to ask you, Mr. Eric: Do you know of any Bosnian Serbs that were walking around the village of Kravica, to your knowledge, within the following days or weeks of the attack?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, if you look at this tape, the date displayed is the 23rd of January, 1993, if it is the correct date, and it should be. Therefore, this is 16 days after Kravica was taken, and the people you can see in the footage are Muslims. These people can't be Serbs, because Kravica was only liberated in March. These people must be Muslims. Q.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you continue the tape, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is my own field. The Kravica Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond cooperative.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Stop there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the cooperative where fruits and vegetables and food were brought before --

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, if you recognise any of the houses in this film --

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: There is Slavorad Vasic's house, Slavorad Vasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Novica Obaskic's house. Miladin Popovic's house. Ranko Cvijetinovic house. Neso Milovanovic's house; my best man. Milos Milanovic's house. Ziko, who lives in Austria, Lazo Pejic's house. Raso Eric's house. He's a relation of mine. This is the school building. And this is my house now, the one without a roof.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your house between the building with a little bit of red on it and then the other building that is lying to the right of the screen? The image is a bit fuzzy. Is that what you're indicating is your house?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, with the video that you've just seen, could you please tell the --

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: But I did recognise it nevertheless.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The video you've just seen, would you say that these were the houses in the state of damage that they were on the 7th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I don't know how the witness is able to say that, unless he's going to go through house by house and say that he saw each of those houses on the day. He's being invited to make a very broad brush assertion that yes indeed every one of those houses was damaged in that state on that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'll reframe the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. You need to rephrase the question in any case, Ms. Sellers. But the problem that I have goes beyond what Mr. Jones has just pointed out, namely, the images are so blurred to start with. And we are fast moving at the same time. Even if we stop and we have stills and ask the witness to look at stills. I mean, we're not going to get anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: There's also been no independent confirmation of the date. The witness said this should be correct. But there's no reason for believing that the date is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Unless we get the person or persons who filmed this to confirm that we're never going to know, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand, and that could be typical questions for cross-examination. What I do want to say is that the witness can speak about whether there was damage, the damage that he's seen on the film, whether that damage in his knowledge was made on the 7th of January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, let's rephrase it and I start and then you can continue Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have indicated to us, Mr. Eric, several of these houses and identified who they belong to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were these houses damaged or destroyed on the 7th of January?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On what basis do you maintain that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you have this tape footage. I can see it here. And the last time I testified, I had a photo of my own house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right. You can proceed on your own now, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would ask that we just roll the part where Mr. Eric said it was his house again, that part of the film.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's supposed to be a roofless house, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, forever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Eric, is that your house in the far background?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would now ask the Trial Chamber -- I'm sorry, the registrar if we could see Exhibit -- it used to be P400. We're going to ask for a new number. It's ERN 01087916.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, do you recognise the picture in front of you? Would you please tell the Trial Chamber what that is a picture of.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: This is my house, my father's house, if you like. This is the house where I grew up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this house damaged on the 7th of January, 1993 in the attack on Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you just recognised a house and the video clip that you said was your house. The house that you referred to in the video clip, is this the same house that we're seeing in the picture now?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise your house in the video clip with the same type of damage that you recognise your house in the picture having?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. It can be seen quite clearly. I think there is no doubt. I would certainly always be able to recognise my own house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would ask that -- Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This photo bearing ERN number 01087916 is being tendered, admitted into evidence, and marked as Prosecution Exhibit P463.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Can we continue the videotape, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the bus station in Kravica. It's around the centre of the village, more or less. The school is in this direction, over there, but this is the sort of centre of the village. The school is a hundred metres further down. Then the medical, the health centre was behind. You can see the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you go back just a bit before this, right after we come across what appears to be a bridge. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, the image that you have on the screen in front of you, could you --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Can we roll back just a little bit more. Thank you. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the building on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There are two buildings, according to me, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. The one to the left-hand side, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: To the left is the house of Zoran Ilic. Afterwards, when it was repaired in 1994, that's where these statements were taken from, on the ground floor, the ones that we saw earlier. And this is the other house of Milos and Svetan [phoen] Popovic. They're brothers. This is the other house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this where the Zvornik film crew filmed you and the others in the house that you're indicating, to the left?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. In this room on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from looking at this house, can you please tell the Trial Chamber whether this house had a roof on it before January 7th, 1993.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, it did. It burned down. It didn't have a concrete ceiling, and that's why it all collapsed. This other house did, so that's why the Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond damage was not the same. The roof did not collapse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in front of the house, did that house look as it does in the film prior to the 7th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. Before January the 7th, it was covered properly. It had a roof. But now you can see that it was burned, and this was filmed on the 23rd of January, so you can see there that the house had been burned.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could we continue, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the house of Drago Radovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Stop for a second, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The house we just saw, did that house have a roof on it prior to the 7th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, it did. Also the local hall had a roof, as well as the post office. They both had roofs before January the 7th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Eric, is this near where you worked in the clinic that you testified about before?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. The clinic is between these two buildings, maybe some ten metres behind this other building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell the Trial Chamber: What is the building on the left-hand side of the screen, and what is the building on the right-hand side that looks as if it's directly in front of us?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: To the left is the cultural hall. That's what we could call it. On the right side is the local municipal office, the post office, and a shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, were these two buildings damaged in the attack of the 7th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the house of Milan Milocevic [phoen], the house of Rajko Milocevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you notice any damage on that house in the film that you're seeing now?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see one is burned down, and you can see that the other one had also been burned and you can see the soot. It's still in that state, more or less, today, and you can see the traces of fire on the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, was that house in that state prior to the 7th of January, 1993? Was it burned like that before?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. It was a very nicely kept house, and you can see here that it was burned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The house of Dragan Saljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, were the damages, to your knowledge, occurring or did they occur on the 7th of January, 1993, of these houses that we're seeing on the video?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: This is the house of Ziko Milovcevic. I made a mistake here. This is the house of Zivojin Milovcevic. The footage is not quite clear, so at first I wasn't quite certain. So this is the house of Zivojin Milovcevic and it burned for a Christmas, on the 7th of January, just like mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, can you make any commentary about the house we're seeing on the film now?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: This is the house of Stanko Grujic. It burned down. Before the 7th of January it had a roof, but now you can see that it has no roof and that it has been burned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And before we proceed any further, it's more clear now than it has ever been before. Witness, if you look just underneath, just below that house, there are some words there in Cyrillic and in capital letters. Can you read them out to us, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. This was probably written by Television Zvornik, and it states "Muslim video footage."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One further question. All along we have been hearing some background music, and also some singing. You have already given us some information on whether you consider this to be Bosnian Muslim music or Bosnian Serb music, and you said that you consider it to be more likely Bosnian Muslim music. Do you have an idea at all what the words that are being sung say? Is this -- is this -- what kind of song is this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a song by the brothers Bajic. They're Muslims, these people. These are not nationalistic songs. This is music that was listened to by Muslims mostly. Our people listened to it as well, but not so much. You can recognise the instruments that are being used. Some of the songs are about love. They mention girls and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you understood exactly where I was aiming, where I was getting. This is not a nationalistic song; it's just pure musical entertainment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. The music is played in the background as they were recording. I guess it was music that was in the vehicle that they were driving in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you. We just have a couple more seconds to go in the video clip. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Mika's house. I cannot remember the last name. No. Grujic. The house of Miko Grujic and of his father over here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these houses destroyed prior to the 7th of January, 1993 or, like all the other houses that you've described, has this occurred, to your opinion, during the attack?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, do you notice whether there is snow on the ground at the time of the filming of this video or not?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I can see snow, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the house of Saljevic Dragan. This is the house of -- I can't remember. The woman's name is Zorka. This is already on the way out of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And can you notice any damage at all on this house?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, you can see that the window frames have been burned, the roof damaged partially. Each house did not burn down completely. Some burned more, some less. But most of them were burned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, do you recognise this house?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. Madzar Saljevic. That is the name of the person. I know him well. You can see this house, how it had burned down. It's a Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond slightly older house that does not have the ceiling concrete layer, so it's easier to burn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, in which direction are we going now, according to the film?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: This is on the way out of Kravica. This is the village of Kajici, in the direction of Bratunac. I think that this footage will just go up until Glogova, not much further than that, and it will end. This is the village of Kajici, and this is the house of my cousin Marko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the road that has been shown on this videotape, is this the road that links Kravica and Bratunac that you testified about earlier?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, after the end of this videotape, there will be no further questions from the Prosecutor. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the house of my cousin Nikolic, Dusko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That house was also destroyed on the 7th of January, 1993, Mr. Eric?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's about -- what's the distance between Kravica and this house of your cousin?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Perhaps a kilometre or so, maybe a little more. About a kilometre, and two, three, five hundred metres, towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these houses that we've seen on today's video, were these how the houses look or appear to you when you re-entered Kravica on the 15th of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps in the meantime, since the 23rd, until March, some houses were destroyed a little more. If the house was new, perhaps the roof was taken apart or something, but it was more or less in this state.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Before I hand you over to the Defence, Mr. Eric, on the 7th of January, was there snow in Kravica and in the surroundings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And where were you on the 23rd of January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 23rd of January, I was in the 2nd Battalion, towards Voljavica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How far were you from Kravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About 15 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would you be in a position to confirm to us whether, on the 23rd of January, there would have been snow still on the ground, on the 23rd of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't really notice that or remember that, but I think so, because we have winters with snow over there. The winter is not like it is here. But I wasn't really following it. I don't remember noticing it. But I think that there was snow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I'm now passing you on to Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Just one thing. I would just like to move the video into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And I would emphasise again for the Prosecution point of view, it's the second part that we've seen today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Has this been pre-marked, Mr. Siller? 448. Thank you. 448 is the first one that we saw? 448 is the first video that we saw, in which the witness appears -- or is it the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: That is all one video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Thank you. All right. So it remains 448. And that has already been tendered and admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: It's been given a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But 448.1 was the transcript. 448.1 is the transcript. Excerpt of the transcript. Just one page. Yes. So the entire video is being tendered and received in evidence and marked as Prosecution Exhibit P448. And to be precise, Ms. Sellers, this has ERN number V000-5206. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. I believe that the number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's 446. That's 446.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: 2774. You'll be receiving copies, I'm informed, at a different time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Madam Vidovic. Would you like to start your cross-examination now or would you like to have the break now? We can start and have the break in ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to put a few questions to him about this video and then we will continue. Cross-examined by Ms. Vidovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Eric.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Earlier you responded to a question by the Prosecutor by saying that on the 7th of January, during the attack, you wore a uniform. That was the old JNA uniform, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, it was more parts of the old JNA uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But nevertheless, a uniform?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: The sweater was civilian, the boots were civilian, also the trousers, so it was half/half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under oath, on the 26th of October, 2004, in response to my question about what you wore and what other people wore during the attack - and this is page 1265, line 25 of the transcript - you said, for example: "I personally, on the 7th of January, wore a civilian uniform." This was not true; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: But I also gave you a paper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you respond to my question, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: I was never a civilian. I was 28 years old. So it makes no sense for me to be a civilian, to be in civilian clothes. Yes, but I couldn't have been a civilian. There was no question of that. Before that, I gave you a paper which said what my engagement was in the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, I would ask you, please, to respond to my questions, as briefly as possible, with yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the transcript of the 26th of October, on page 1265, under oath, you said that on that day you wore civilian clothing. That was not true, was it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: It was more civilian clothing rather than military clothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But today you described that you were wearing a military jacket.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. When we were leaving to be evacuated, I put the jacket on because outside it was cold. But you can see what it looked like on the 7th of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic and Mr. Eric, and this is the last time I'm going to say this. You are not allowing an interval of time between question and answer. You're not even allowing -- Ms. Vidovic is not allowing the witness to even finish his question, and the witness is not allowing Ms. Vidovic to finish her question. So we can't go on like this. If you continue like this, I will have to stop the cross-examination. I'm making it very clear. Yes, Madam Vidovic, please repeat your question. And you, Mr. Eric, allow her to finish her question, allowing enough time for the interpreters to translate to us in English and to others in French. Yes, Madam Vidovic. Could you repeat your question. And I would suggest if you are referring the witness to a particular part of the transcript of the sitting of the 26th or 23rd of October, that you bring that out and you read precisely what he said. Because I do remember he gave more details about his clothing than what you're putting to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, I am now going to read to you a part of your testimony on page 1226 of the 26th of October of 2004. To the question of His Honour Judge Brydensholt, you answered -- the Judge asked you: "Were people wearing uniforms?" "I saw that about 150 uniforms remained on the 7th of January." "Did the guards from uniforms on the 7th of January?" You answered: "No. For example, I personally, on the 7th of January, wore civilian clothes. I had a shirt, which was part of the JNA uniform." My question is: You said today: "I had a shirt, I had trousers, and I had a jacket."

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that you had an olive-drab jacket.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also, you had an olive-drab shirt and olive-drab trousers; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic, and I never said that I was a civilian. Let's be clear about this, but that I was a soldier, and I gave you a paper about my participation in the war. So there is nothing in dispute about that. We're talking about parts of clothing, and if this is important, we can go into this in detail very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are talking about uniforms here. Also, today you said that you received from the JNA in Kravica about 100 to 150 uniforms.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Maybe more or maybe less. We're talking about old JNA uniforms. That is correct. There were also boots, belts, the odd shirts, and so on, cap.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Mr. Eric. During the footage that we were shown, you said that this music that we heard is more customary for Muslims.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it so that the Bajic Brothers actually recorded their music in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know where they recorded the music, but they're listeners were mostly Muslims. I don't know where they recorded their music in the former Yugoslavia, but I remember well -- I mean, it's a good thing that I remember that it was them who were singing. I don't know. It's possible that they recorded their music in Belgrade. That's something that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you say that this is music that was listened to by the Muslims? What do you base that on?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, this is something that I know. I know that in my area, I grew up with Muslims, near Muslims, and they usually listen to that music. They listen to other music as well, but this kind of music was something that mostly Muslims listened to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Witness. Today you were shown a series of houses. Did you see those houses burning on the 7th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't able to see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you conclude that they were burned based on the footage that we saw?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, I know that they were set on fire on the 7th. When we went back in March, this is what the houses looked like. So I don't know when else they could have been burned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw those houses in March, and you saw them now, in this footage. It's true, isn't it, that you did not see them burning?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, you cannot really see that. Sandici is far away. It wasn't possible to see that. I couldn't even see the centre of the village. You could see smoke from the surrounding hills. You couldn't see them burning from the direction in which we were evacuating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time when you were being shown the footage, you saw the date 23rd of January, 1993, and you said that that should have been the date.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: It was the date for sure. I am sure of that now. I saw this tape before. I saw it as part of the Zvornik TV broadcast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on what are you sure that this was recorded on the 23rd of January? Were you there when this programme was recorded?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. Excuse me. But in January 1992, we were in Kravica, also in 1991; 1991 and 1992. Then we were there in 1993, in March; and in 1994; and since then we were there all the time. So this damage could have been caused only in that period, because that's when the Muslims were in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the footage you saw a group of people, and you said: "These are Muslims."

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Those people could not have been Serbs, not at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you agree that those people were civilians?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: You can't see very clearly. There may have been fighters among them, civilians too. Maybe they were looting, maybe they were just passing through. I really can't say what exactly they were doing. I can't say anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I'll just ask you this question: Mr. Eric, is it possible that it was precisely those people that you saw in the footage were going around taking roofs off houses, removing woodwork and, generally speaking, looting, as you said?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. This is pure speculation, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't answer the question, Mr. Eric. Shall we have the break now?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed we can, Your Honour. I'll continue later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's proceed. And once more, may I appeal to both of you, Mr. Eric in particular, but also Ms. Vidovic, to allow an interval between question and answer. Madam Vidovic, you may proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, whenever possible, please answer yes, no, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is true, isn't it, that in the area, the SDS held a promotional rally in Kravica, of all places, at that time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that not mean that it was precisely in Kravica that it had a lot of support and supporters who supported the party platform?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is true, isn't it, that the SDS was in control of the Crisis Staff in order to secure the implementation of its own policies?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: This is not something that I'm aware of. I don't think I can answer this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Madam Vidovic, because I think we need to be clear about this. The idea of recalling this witness was not to put to him questions that you could easily have put when he was here in October, and you didn't. The whole idea is to put -- was to put to him questions that you couldn't have possibly put to him on the 26th of October, because the videotape that we've seen earlier was not available then. So these last two questions you could have easily put to him in October, and you didn't. So I will -- you know exactly what I mean. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Your Honour, may I be allowed to respond? This footage was the first time I learned during Mr. Jovan Nikolic's interview, which is part of the footage, that an SDS promotional rally in the area was held in Kravica. Furthermore, certain persons are referred to that are related to the SDS and the Crisis Staff. We didn't know about that, because if we had known about that, I certainly would have asked the question. In addition to that, except for Mr. Jovan Nikolic, several other people are interviewed in the footage. Mr. Rase Milanovic [phoen], for example, is bringing up issues that are of great relevance to our defence, and this is another thing that we knew nothing about at the time. That is why we remain adamant that we should pursue this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's fair enough. Thank you, Madam Vidovic. You may proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, the last time around you testified that you were a member of the Crisis Staff establishment-wise, in terms of your establishment rank, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were other people who were members of the Crisis Staff in the same way as you, according to their establishment rank, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness nods.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You -- do you know Mr. Luka Bogdanovic, who is another person from the area and he's a well-known person, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Madam Vidovic. When the interpreter -- when the witness nods instead of answering yes, what I would like to see or what I would like to have in place is not what we have now, in other words, we get a record in the transcript by the interpreter saying the witness nods. What I would like to see is that the interpreter draw my attention that they haven't heard the witness say yes or no, and then we'll ask the witness to answer the question. Because this is the interpreter's interpretation of what the witness supposedly is doing, and we need a specific answer, yes or no. So the question was, Mr. Eric, that there were other people who were members of the Crisis Staff in the same way as you were, according to their establishment rank, weren't there? What did you answer, or what did you want to answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe if I re-ask the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. You should start even with the question before, with the prior one; in other words, whether it is true that he himself was member of the Crisis Staff on the basis of his rank or his position.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a member of the Crisis Staff, based on your establishment rank?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were other persons too, weren't there, who were members of the Crisis Staff, based on their establishment ranks, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Probably. Yes, they must have been members too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know Mr. Luka Bogdanovic, don't you? He comes from the same area?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He too was a member of the Kravica Crisis Staff at the same time as you were, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Maybe it was recorded that way, but he wasn't. I don't really know. I didn't really go to those meetings very often myself. I was under no obligation to attend, so I went maybe three times altogether. But only in relation to my own specific duties. Therefore, I don't really know who attended or when they met. I simply wasn't interested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Luka Bogdanovic attend meetings of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't know. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, can he tell us how often the Crisis Staff met at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure which period of time they met in. I really didn't follow the situation. If I had known at that time that I would need the information one day, I would have been more interested. I was more involved with the medical centre, because that was my specific duty. I'm not a curious person by nature. Therefore, I really can't answer that question. I'm afraid if I give you an answer, I might go wrong. Therefore, I think I'm better off remaining silent on the issue, if I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, or rather, it is correct, isn't it, that Luka Bogdanovic was a member of the Crisis Staff as a representative of the police, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, not really. I hardly ever saw him in Kravica. He was in the civilian police at the time, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain why it was that you said he maybe was recorded there, but he was not a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: That may be what the book says. The writer from the last time, Boro Miljanovic, that he recorded him as a member of the Crisis Staff, but I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I have the usher's assistance now, please. I would like to place a public security station Bratunac document on the ELMO. Can you please just show the witness this document, and can it please be placed on the ELMO. The document bears the following number: 01320218. This is a public security station document, a list of workers who, in April, performed duties at the public security station during the month of April and who should be paid in advance for this month. Your Honours, page 1 bears salaries for May 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at this document carefully, especially the first two names on the list. The first name is Mr. Milutin Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: The deceased Milutin Milosevic. That's correct. The next name is Bogdanovic Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct, isn't it, he is listed here as a komandir. It is true, isn't it, that Mr. Luka Bogdanovic was a close associate of the late Milutin Milosevic, was he not?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: They were both members of the police. Now, as to whether they were close associates or not, I really can't venture a guess there. I can't say. I've never thought about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can you now please look at this list, and can you now turn to the last page, please. It's true, isn't it, that this list contains 136 names?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that this Bratunac public security station unit from April 1992 to the events in January 1993 took part in coordinated military activity in the Kravica area?

utterances.speaker: SLAVISA ERIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: I have no idea. I don't know. I don't think so, though. But I can't be sure. I don't know. As simple as that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, please. For the record, Madam Vidovic, although you have suggested to the witness that this list contains 136 names and he seems to have agreed with you, in reality, from what I can establish, having a look at this, there are two handwritten -- additional handwritten names, and that would bring the total to 138. Correct me if I'm wrong, but I don't think I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 137.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you're quite right. 137 would be the correct number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you tell me 137, I'm quite right, you're not telling me something that is correct. There is an additional name on the last page, Djokanovic Radojko, and on the previous page, at the bottom of the page, there is -- I can't read the name. Milovan Milanovic [phoen], Milovan Milanovic. Yes. Which basically would add to 138. I don't see any of the other names being struck off. They are all there. All right? We are agreed on that?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're quite right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's just for the record. Yes. Judge Eser would like to put a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
